implementation_statement: No access policy existed. POL-02 (P06), approved 2026-08-31 and effective 2026-09-01, covers HMI, PLC, remote, and vendor access. A one-page OT account procedure (who gets which HMI and remote access, and how it is removed) is due 2026-10-31.

The Chief Operator creates HMI and remote monitoring accounts; the MSP creates business accounts at the Office Manager's request. Gap: one shared HMI login and one shared remote desktop password; no rule for changing shared passwords when someone leaves (a former operator knew the remote password until 2026-07-22); no periodic review.
evidence: HMI user list; remote monitoring user list; remote desktop tool settings; termination record of the former operator

implementation_statement: The HMI software enforces view, operate, and administer levels. Gap: everyone signs in with the shared operator login, so the operate level cannot be tied to a person; the PLC accepts program changes from any device on the network.
Office staff have no local administrator rights (MSP standard). Gap: the shared HMI login runs with administrator rights on the HMI computer; the remote desktop tool runs with full control.
evidence: MSP endpoint policy; HMI computer local accounts

implementation_statement: Remote access to the HMI is through a commercial remote desktop tool in unattended mode, relayed by the tool vendor's cloud service, which encrypts the session. Gap: always on, one shared password, no MFA, no approval per session, used from personal devices, and no review of the connection log. Target: attended access only, named accounts with MFA, and Chief Operator approval for each vendor session by 2026-09-30.
evidence: Remote desktop tool console; P07 test

implementation_statement: One MSP-managed Wi-Fi network with WPA2 encryption. Gap: the Wi-Fi password is shared with visitors and contractors and reaches the same network as the HMI computer and PLC.
evidence: Firewall and access point configuration export

implementation_statement: No security awareness training or phishing exercise has been held. Annual training for all 7 staff plus quarterly phishing simulations through the MSP start 2026-10 (POL-02 Part C).
No OT security training for operators. A free EPA or CISA water-sector course for the 3 licensed operators is planned by 2026-12-31, covering remote access, HMI changes, and reporting.

provider_if_inherited: Remote desktop tool vendor; remote monitoring vendor
implementation_statement: The HMI alarm and event list records alarms and some operator actions; the remote desktop tool vendor keeps a 90-day connection history; the remote monitoring service logs sign-ins. Gap: no defined list of events to log; HMI setpoint changes are not tied to a person.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Nobody reviews the remote desktop connection history, remote monitoring sign-ins, or HMI events. Weekly review of remote connections and monthly review of HMI changes start 2026-10 (POL-02 B.8).
An independent OT security consultant assessed 13 controls on 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-12 (P07). The company will repeat an independent assessment every 2 years and a self-review each year (POL-02 A.6).
No baseline configuration of the HMI computer, PLC, or modems. A one-page baseline per device (firmware, settings, open ports, accounts) is due with the inventory, 2026-10-31.

The PLC program can be changed only with the programming software on the HMI computer or the integrator's laptop. Gap: no PLC program password; key switch left in remote-program; no approval rule for integrator changes.

The office firewall blocks unsolicited inbound traffic. Gap: the remote desktop tool and the remote monitoring gateway make outbound connections from the plant network with no restriction; the tank modem's web administration was open to the internet (closed 2026-08-12).

No current OT inventory. The integrator's 2018 drawings list the PLC, RTUs, and HMI computer but not the modems, gateway, or firmware. Inventory of every OT component, with firmware and network address, due 2026-10-31.

The 2023 emergency plan covers hurricanes and power loss, with contacts, generator steps, and the boil water template. Gap: no cyber section beyond 'call the SCADA integrator'; manual operation steps not written. A cyber annex based on P08 and written hand-operation steps are due 2026-10-31.

Hand operation was used for real in October 2024 but never exercised on purpose; no restore test of any backup. An annual hand-operation drill and a cyber tabletop with the integrator and MSP are due 2026-11-30.

The MSP backs up the productivity suite and 2 office desktops nightly to a cloud backup service, never restore-tested. The remote monitoring service keeps 2 years of trend history. Gap: no company copy of the PLC program, HMI project, or HMI computer image.

No documented way to rebuild the HMI computer or reload the PLC. A recovery procedure with the integrator (rebuild media, verified PLC program, return from hand mode one process at a time) is due 2026-11-30.

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite, billing, and accounting SaaS vendors
implementation_statement: Unique accounts for email, billing, and accounting. Gap: HMI and remote desktop access use shared credentials, so actions cannot be tied to a person.
evidence: Suite user export; HMI user list

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite, billing, and accounting SaaS vendors
implementation_statement: MFA is enforced on email for all users and on the billing and accounting systems. Gap: no MFA on the remote desktop tool, the remote monitoring service, or the MSP-held firewall login.

Email and SaaS passwords follow the suite policy. Gap: HMI administrator and PLC passwords unchanged since 2018; tank modem default password (changed 2026-08-12); device passwords kept in a spreadsheet all staff can open.
No incident handling capability beyond calling the integrator. The P08 runbook, approved 2026-08-31, sets out containment (hand mode first), analysis, recovery, and lessons learned.

Operators report plant problems to the Chief Operator by phone, and the company reports violations to the primacy agency. Gap: no rule for reporting suspected cyber events; no contacts for the FBI, CISA, or the insurer in the plant binder. POL-03 (P06) and the P08 matrix add them.
No incident response plan existed at fieldwork. The P08 runbook for an HMI remote-access compromise was approved 2026-08-31 and will be printed for the plant binder by 2026-09-15.
The SCADA integrator maintains the HMI and PLC remotely through the remote desktop tool. Gap: sessions are not approved or watched, not logged by the company, and use the shared password.
evidence: Remote desktop tool console; integrator interview 2026-07-21

implementation_statement: Fence and locked gate at the plant; keyed doors; the plant building intrusion alarm is monitored by an alarm company and also wired to the alarm dialer; Well 3 and the tank are fenced and padlocked. Keys are held by the 3 operators, the Utility Field Technician, and the Owner.
This SSP, approved 2026-08-31, is the company's first written description of the WTSS and its controls. It is reviewed every August.

baseline: Not in High baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The Owner designated the Office Manager as security and compliance coordinator in writing on 2026-08-31, with the Chief Operator responsible for OT security decisions.

Termination is handled by the Office Manager with a payroll checklist. Gap: the checklist does not cover shared passwords, the remote desktop tool, the remote monitoring service, or keys. The termination checklist covering all of them is due 2026-09-30.
First written risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 using NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01), with the BIA (P05). Updated every July and after major changes, including the subdivision connection.

No vulnerability scanning. The company will enroll in CISA's free vulnerability scanning for internet-facing addresses by 2026-09-30 and review OT advisories for its HMI, PLC, and modem models each month.

External services are listed in section 8. Gap: the integrator, remote monitoring vendor, and MSP contracts have no security terms; the MSP contract excludes plant control systems. Security terms at renewal or by addendum, due 2026-12-31.

The MSP-managed firewall separates the site from the internet. Gap: inside, the HMI computer, PLC, gateway, and office computers share one flat network. A separate OT network behind its own firewall rules, with the gateway as the only outbound path, is due 2026-11-30.

The hypochlorite pump's mechanical stroke setting caps output at about 2.5 times the normal rate whatever the PLC commands; the chlorine analyzer's own relays call the on-call phone through the alarm dialer; every well, pump, and the chemical feed has a hand-off-auto switch. SCADA cannot override these.

The MSP patches office computers monthly. Gap: the HMI computer has had no operating system or SCADA software updates since May 2024 and is outside the MSP contract; modem and PLC firmware never reviewed. A patch plan agreed with the integrator, tested before installation, due 2026-12-31.
evidence: MSP patch report; HMI computer update history

implementation_statement: MSP-managed antivirus on office computers. Gap: the HMI computer has only the built-in operating system protection with no one checking it.

Process alarms reach the on-call phone through the remote monitoring service and the alarm dialer, and operators watch process values. Gap: no monitoring for unauthorized access or changes; the anomaly detection feature is a process tool on trial, not a security monitor (P10).
evidence: Alarm dialer test log; remote monitoring settings
